title: Ecommerce Business Report
description: Sales, products, customers and fulfillment across every tenant, in one view.

generation.instructions: Act as a professional data analyst for an ecommerce company. Write short messages, max 255 characters. Explain what stands behind the numbers (categories, brands, customer segments, countries, order outcomes) more than restating the numbers themselves.

sections.title: Sales Performance
sections.description: How net sales and gross profit developed over the period.

children.markdown:
How net sales and gross profit developed over the period.

**In this chapter:** At a Glance  ·  Category Mix

Read revenue against order volume: revenue rising faster than orders means a higher average basket.

Watch for peaks that are not repeated the next month.

**Ask:** is growth coming from more customers or bigger orders?
Which categories bring in net sales, and how this year compares with last.
**Total Net Sales: Current vs. Last Year**

A few categories usually carry most of the sales.

Gaps between the current and previous period show seasonality or real change.

**Ask:** which category drives the year-on-year difference?

sections.title: Products & Brands
sections.description: Which products and brands drive sales, profit and returns.

children.markdown:
Which products and brands drive sales, profit and returns.

**In this chapter:** Top Performers  ·  Profit & Returns
The products and brands that sell and earn the most.

Best sellers are not always the most profitable.

Brands high on volume but low on profit point to discounting.

**Ask:** where should promotion budget go?
Where gross profit is earned, and which categories come back.

A category with a high return rate gives back part of its profit.

Compare each category's share of profit with its share of returns.

**Ask:** which returns are a product issue and which a sizing or description issue?

sections.title: Customers
sections.description: Who buys, how often, and where they are.

children.markdown:
Who buys, how often, and where they are.

**In this chapter:** Customer Health  ·  Geography & Top Customers
How many customers buy, and how loyal they are.

Retention and repeat orders matter more than new sign-ups.

A dip in weekly activity often comes before a drop in sales.

**Ask:** what brings first-time buyers back for a second order?
Where customers are, and who spends the most.
**Sales and Active Customers by Customer Country**

Countries with many customers but low sales are an upsell opportunity.

Check how much revenue depends on the top 10 customers.

**Ask:** how exposed are we to a few large buyers?

sections.title: Orders & Fulfillment
sections.description: How orders move from placement to completion.

children.markdown:
How orders move from placement to completion.

**In this chapter:** Fulfillment Funnel  ·  Completed vs. Canceled
How orders move from placement to completion.

The biggest step down in the funnel is where orders are lost.

**Ask:** is the drop-off in payment, stock or delivery?
Order outcomes over time and by state.

Cancellation spikes usually line up with stock-outs or delivery delays.

**Ask:** do the top states also have the most cancellations?
What the four chapters add up to.
**Grow the basket, not just the base**
Push the categories and brands that combine volume with margin.
Retention and repeat purchases are the cheapest growth lever.
Fix the funnel step with the biggest drop-off and track cancellations weekly.
